the survival of E. coli K-12 populations in the presence of the R-factor-coded enzymes is due to variations in the resistance level of individual cells.

(i) R-factor-mediated drug-metabolizing enzymes affect the survival of Escherichiacoli K-12 in the presence of antibiotics; (ii) this survival is due to detoxification, variations in resistance, or both; (iii) the R-factor-mediated drug metabolizing enzymes affect the outer membrane permeability; and (iv) the rate of R-factor-mediated drug metabolism decreases with time
R-factor-mediated enzymes affect the survival of the population by (a) metabolizing the drugs, (b) causing lysis, and (c) causing excretion of enzymes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of drug-metabolizing enzymes on the survival and growth of bacterial populations in the presence of antibiotics and with the effect of high drug concentrations on the outer membrane of the cells.
the effect of R-factor-mediated drug-metabolizing enzymes on the survival in the presence of the drugs.
the effect of drug metabolism on the survival of E. coli K-12 and the possible role of drug metabolites as signals for cell division.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
R-factors can cause the survival of cells in high antibiotic concentrations by detoxification of the antibiotic and/or by the presence of mutants.
the R-factor-mediated drug-metabolizing enzymes are responsible for the observed effects on the survival of the bacterial population.
the R-factor-mediated drug-metabolizing enzymes have a significant effect on the survival of E. coli K-12 populations in the presence of antibiotics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
R-factor-mediated drug resistance is not due to the presence and activity of drug-metabolizing enzymes in a single cell.
in the presence of antibiotics the survival of a population is determined by the rate of detoxification of the drug, the number of mutants present in the population, and the rate of cell division.
R-factors are not only responsible for the resistance of cells to antibiotics, but they also have a profound influence on the growth and survival of the cell population.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to consider the effect of detoxification on antibiotic survival curves and to use the proper control for the inoculum effect.
R-factors are not just a means for bacteria to acquire resistance but also a means of survival in the presence of antibiotics.
the presence of drug metabolizing enzymes can affect the survival of the cell population.
